title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's §5 'Retour sur le principe de chirurgie conforme'. He wants to replace the local lemmas 2–3 (behind his Theorem 4 on cutting and regluing conformal surfaces) by global lemmas of uniformization type. This page states 'Lemme 1', part A.

Setting. V is the bounded component of C∖C, where C is a Jordan curve. I is a topological arc with endpoints a and b, such that I∩C={b} and I∖{b}⊂V. Let U=V∖I be the slit Jordan domain, so ∂U=C∪I. Assume also that C and I are rectifiable.

On the unit circle take the points 1, ζ=e^{2πi/3} and ζ̄. They cut ∂D into three arcs: α from ζ to ζ̄ through −1, β from 1 to ζ, and β̄ from 1 to ζ̄.

Claim. There is a continuous map f: D̄→C with four properties:
(1) f restricted to the open disc is a homeomorphism onto U.
(2) f(ζ)=f(ζ̄)=b, and f maps α∖{ζ,ζ̄} homeomorphically onto C∖{b}.
(3) f|β and f|β̄ are bijections onto I, so f(1)=a, the tip of the slit. The arcs β and β̄ are the two 'banks' (prime-end sides) of the slit.
(4) f is holomorphic on D.
In other words, f is the Riemann map of the slit domain, extended to the closed disc. It presents D̄ as the closed disc V̄ cut open along I.

Next page. f is unique because Aut(D) acts simply transitively on positively ordered triples on S¹. Composing the two boundary bijections gives a canonical homeomorphism φ=(f|β̄)^{-1}∘(f|β): β→β̄ with φ(1)=1 and φ(ζ)=ζ̄. Part B then claims the converse: every ('rectifiable') homeomorphism φ: β≅β̄ arises in this way. That is, the closed disc with β glued to β̄ by φ carries a conformal structure realizing it as a slit disc.

In modern terms this is the conformal welding homeomorphism of a slit, i.e. the two-sided boundary correspondence of a slit map. Grothendieck intends to use welding (cutting a disc open along an arc and regluing) as the global tool for conformal surgery on Riemann surfaces.
errors: The rectifiability hypotheses are unnecessary for part A. The Riemann map onto U=V∖I extends continuously to D̄ by Carathéodory's theorem, because ∂U is locally connected; each point of I∖{a,b} corresponds to exactly two prime ends and a to one.

On the next page (part B), 'rectifiable' is not the right hypothesis for the converse. Any monotone homeomorphism between arcs is automatically of bounded variation, so the condition is essentially vacuous. Yet not every homeomorphism is a conformal welding (Oikawa, Vainio), and uniqueness can also fail (Bishop's flexible curves). The standard sufficient condition is quasisymmetry (Lehto–Virtanen; Pfluger) or something weaker such as Lehto's condition. So the converse as written is false or at least unjustified.
The parenthetical writes the boundary as the dotted symbol 'U̇', meaning ∂U; it is correct, but the phrase 'on suppose I∪C=∂U' is really a consequence of the hypotheses, not an extra assumption.
The NB refers to 'a) b) c)' while the conditions are numbered 1), 2), 3): a minor labelling slip.

ideas.what: Extension of the Riemann map of a slit Jordan domain to the closed disc, with the boundary circle split into three arcs (outer curve, two banks of the slit) normalized by 1, e^{±2πi/3}
ideas.modern_name: Carathéodory extension / prime ends for slit domains

ideas.what: Canonical homeomorphism φ between the two banks of the slit (welding map), and the claimed converse that every homeomorphism φ arises
ideas.modern_name: Conformal welding (here of a slit / 'self-welding' of two boundary arcs)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pfluger (1960), Lehto–Virtanen (1960), Oikawa (1961); slit welding in the Loewner/zipper literature (Marshall–Rohde), SLE welding (Sheffield 2016)

ideas.what: Uniqueness via simple transitivity of Aut(D) on positively ordered triples of boundary points
ideas.modern_name: Three-point normalization of Möbius automorphisms of the disc

ideas.what: Using global uniformization/welding statements as the foundation of a 'principle of conformal surgery' for cutting and regluing Riemann surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Douady–Hubbard (c. 1985, polynomial-like maps), Shishikura; welding-based surgery in Teichmüller theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1983–84 conformal-surgery programme is built on the slit welding homeomorphism φ: β→β̄, the two-sided boundary correspondence of a slit map. This is precisely the object later central to the Loewner/zipper and SLE conformal welding literature. It is an independent, contemporaneous appearance of welding as a surgery tool, linked to his combinatorial/Teichmüller interests (Esquisse era), but mathematically known.
missed.quote: f|β et f|β̄ induisent des bijections de β et β̄ sur I
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it documents Grothendieck reaching conformal welding as a surgery tool around the time of quasiconformal surgery in dynamics. No new theorem is involved, and his converse requires a quasisymmetry-type hypothesis he did not identify.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful statement of a classical fact (Carathéodory extension for a slit Jordan domain), set up to define the welding map. The interesting part is the context, Grothendieck independently building surgery on conformal welding, but the mathematics is standard. The converse on the next page is stated with an inadequate hypothesis.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit supposons de plus' should read 'Supposons de plus que C et I soient rectifiables. Soit a l'autre extrémité de I.'

'est {+réunion de+} l'union [?]' is better rendered as: the frontier 'est réunion d'une courbe de Jordan C et d'un intervalle topologique I tel que...'. The struck words were 'rectifiable. Alors il existe une fonction continue' and probably 'homéomorphe'/'holomorphe'.
'$\dot U$' in '(on suppose I∪C=U̇)' denotes the boundary ∂U.
The inserted word read as 'itération' is doubtful. From context it is a word like 'incision'/'découpage' (f presents D̄ as the disc Ū=V̄ cut open along I); 'itération' makes no sense here.
'(ζ = exp 2iπ/3 ...)': the arcs α, β, β̄ are determined by 1, ζ, ζ̄; the left figure shows α containing −1 and β̄ near ζ̄, consistent with the transcription.
The '73' at the bottom left is an archival folio number, not mathematics.
